newsitem.title: CUBA: Argentina's Pescetti wins Casa de las Americas prize.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Pescetti wins Casa de las Americas prize.

text.p: Argentina's Luis Maria Pescetti on Thursday won Cuba's annual Casa de las Americas (Americas House) prize for the best novel from Latin America for his "El Ciudadano de Mis Zapatos" (The Citizen of My Shoes), the organisers said.
The jury said in its citation that Pescetti had successfully woven the story of a family tragedy into a vivid portrayal of social life and politics in Argentina in the 1980s.

Ronaldo Menendez Plasencia of Cuba won the short story category with his collection "El Derecho al Pataleo de los Ahorcados (The Right of the Hung Men to Kick) while Cuban Ramon Fajardo Estrada won the non-fiction prize for his biography of Cuban singer and actress Rita Montaner.

Angela Leite de Souza won a special prize for Brazilian literature with her poetry "Estas Muitas Minas" (These Many Mines), while Cuban-American Sonia Rivera-Valdes won a special award for Hispanic literature in the United States with her short story collection "Las historias prohibidas de Marta Veneranda" (The Forbidden Stories of Marta Veneranda).

The literature prizes are awarded each year by the Casa de las Americas, a foundation for the promotion of Latin America literature set up after Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution. This year the jury of 21 writers and intellectuals from 10 countries picked prizes from some 560 manuscripts from 22 countries.
